metadata.title: airoute V1 Implementation Walkthrough
metadata.summary: A source-backed walkthrough of airoute's deterministic, quality-first router for native AI coding-agent CLIs at commit 03d6c8e53bec7c689cca0a8aa1fce269c1802fc0.

blocks.markdown: airoute V1 is a local TypeScript/Node 20 CLI that classifies task text, builds an eligible provider set, ranks routes deterministically, explains the choice, and launches the selected official native CLI. It is subscription-aware without proxying model traffic or reading OAuth tokens. The canonical statement is `README.md:1-9`; the safety contract is `docs/SPEC.md:1-22`.

blocks.text: Non-goals are as important as features: V1 is not a model API proxy, daemon, workflow orchestrator, worktree manager, quota scraper, autonomous policy tuner, or generic executable-plugin host.

rows: Pure local classification and deterministic ranking
Sanitized NDJSON facts plus atomic provider projection
Built-in typed adapters; executable plugins deferred

items: Read task text from an argument or stdin and normalize it locally (`src/cli.ts:126-134`, `src/classifier.ts:39-41`).
Classify role, complexity, risk, domain, scope, reasoning, confidence, and explainable lexical signals (`src/classifier.ts:9-111`).
Merge global and repository TOML configuration, then combine adapter declarations, executable presence, and provider-state projection (`src/config.ts:43-78`, `src/cli.ts:85-123`).
Filter mode capabilities and optional provider overrides before deterministic policy ranking (`src/cli.ts:147-183`).
For a run, record a sanitized decision, construct separate executable and argv values, and supervise the immediate child (`src/cli.ts:231-302`, `src/adapters.ts:194-219`, `src/runner.ts:51-108`).
Append sanitized outcomes and only record fallback after a replay-safe pre-execution admission switch (`src/cli.ts:292-313`).

blocks.markdown: The modules are intentionally narrow: classifier and policy are pure; adapter declarations own native contracts and fit priors; runner owns process/fallback safety; store owns durable facts; CLI composes them. `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:21-29` documents this ownership map.

`TaskProfile` is a versioned typed record with role, complexity, risk, domain, scope, reasoning, confidence, and signals (`src/types.ts:1-27`). `classifyTask` uses bounded weighted lexical rules, Unicode normalization, explicit negated-write handling, and deterministic tie-breaking by score then role name (`src/classifier.ts:9-40`).

blocks.text: This is a transparent heuristic classifier, not semantic understanding. Its confidence reflects matched signals, not calibrated probability. User flags can override role or force read-only admission, but capability checks still apply.

blocks.markdown: Tests pin representative edge cases: deterministic broad migrations, negated writes, broad redesign, typo fixes, and debugging risk (`test/classifier.test.ts:4-58`).

Policy version `airoute.quality-first.v1` computes quality from task fit, reasoning, domain, and scope with weights 35%, 25%, 20%, and 20%. The displayed total score is 80% quality and 20% availability (`src/policy.ts:3,19-42`). Selection is deliberately stricter than simply sorting that total: materially lower-quality candidates stay behind, while availability can reorder only candidates within `quality_tolerance`, default 0.05 (`src/policy.ts:44-54`, `src/config.ts:14-19`).

blocks.code:
quality = 0.35·fit + 0.25·reasoning + 0.20·domain + 0.20·scope
display total = 0.80·quality + 0.20·availability
selection = quality band first; availability breaks ties inside tolerance

blocks.markdown: `test/policy.test.ts:45-92` verifies materially better quality wins, balancing happens inside tolerance, unknown quota is neutral, and ineligible routes never re-enter selection. Scores are configurable priors rather than universal model claims (`README.md:48-55`).

blocks.markdown: The complete declarations are `src/adapters.ts:26-148`. Active/dormant status is data (`defaultEnabled`), not prose: Cursor is false at `src/adapters.ts:125-128`, and the candidate builder combines that default with explicit configuration at `src/cli.ts:95-108`. Thus executable presence alone cannot activate a dormant route. `test/adapters.test.ts:10-16` and `test/policy.test.ts:82-92` preserve this boundary.

blocks.text: Adapters declare native argv, capability, probes, aliases, and quality/domain priors. They do not decide availability balancing; that remains in policy and CLI composition.

sections.title: Safe process launching and environment handling

blocks.markdown: `prepareLaunch` returns a typed `PreparedLaunch` with executable and argv separated, `shell: false`, a sanitized environment, and a manual-prompt marker (`src/types.ts:69-75`, `src/adapters.ts:194-219`). `spawnSupervised` passes those values directly to `child_process.spawn`, inherits stdio for native terminal behavior, forwards SIGINT/SIGTERM to the immediate child, and removes listeners when complete (`src/runner.ts:51-108`). No shell string or `eval` is involved.

Environment sanitization removes known direct-model API keys and endpoint overrides while retaining PATH, HOME, terminal variables, native config homes, and keychain access needed by official subscription authentication (`src/adapters.ts:150-169`). The hostile-looking task fixture in `test/adapters.test.ts:39-62` proves quotes and shell metacharacters remain one argv element, and `test/adapters.test.ts:81-90` verifies credential override removal.

blocks.text: Some native CLIs require task text in argv, which same-user process inspection or OS audit tooling may observe. Sensitive tasks should use interactive native entry where possible. Airoute forwards signals only to the immediate child; the harness owns descendants.

sections.title: Read-only fallback versus write stop and no replay

blocks.markdown: `executeWithFallback` encodes the boundary in this order: success returns; any started failure raises `PARTIAL_EXECUTION`; any write-risk pre-start failure raises `SWITCH_APPROVAL_REQUIRED`; read-only fallback continues only for quota, auth, or missing-executable admission failures (`src/runner.ts:11-48`). `spawnSupervised` trusts an admission outcome as pre-start only when the adapter declares the exact exit code (`src/runner.ts:84-100`). `test/runner.test.ts:14-86` covers all three branches and the declared-code requirement.

sections.title: Private sanitized event and state model

blocks.markdown: State is outside repositories under the platform state directory (`src/config.ts:32-41`). The store creates its root with mode 0700, appends `airoute.event.v1` NDJSON with file mode 0600, and atomically replaces `providers.json` through a same-directory temporary file (`src/store.ts:23-45,72-97`).

blocks.markdown: `recordDecision` explicitly deletes `rawPrompt` before append (`src/store.ts:48-52`), while the public type never contains it (`src/types.ts:109-118`). `test/store.test.ts:7-25` checks the versioned envelope and absence of raw prompt data.

History, event export, observed metrics, and deterministic policy replay expose evidence without granting self-modification (`src/cli.ts:378-440,471-515`). Metrics explicitly warn that observed outcomes are not counterfactual; replay changes selection under current policy but cannot estimate unchosen outcomes.

blocks.markdown: The strict Zod proposal schema is `src/proposal.ts:3-29`; validation returns data but never applies changes (`src/proposal.ts:31-34`, `src/cli.ts:516-522`). `test/proposal.test.ts:4-33` accepts an evidence-gated approval-only proposal and rejects automatic promotion or insufficient evidence.

The clean Git history contains five commits, each carrying the same `Amp-Thread-ID` trailer, showing the implementation and hardening cycle was performed through Amp in an AgentX repository context. The current documentation dogfood also runs inside an Amp orb: the orb verified the supplied source archive, loaded the newly built `generating-internal-docs` skill, inspected source/history, authored this semantic JSON, and invoked only the deterministic local compiler. No nested provider CLI was launched.

blocks.markdown: Additional intentional limits: no arbitrary executable adapters before signing/versioning/security semantics; no counterfactual outcome inference; no auto-applied proposals; no claimed ACP for Antigravity; and no replay after ambiguous execution. See `README.md:69-84`, `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:21-29`, and `docs/SMOKE.md:14-18`.

items: Use a disposable repository and install with Node 20 or newer; run `npm ci` and `npm run check` before linking the CLI.
Run `airoute providers --json` and confirm Cursor is disabled by default even if `agent` exists.
Run `airoute doctor --json`; inspect only official status/auth probe results. Treat `unknown` as unknown, not success or available quota.
Run `airoute explain` on representative read-only, localized-write, and broad-write text; verify profile signals and quality-band ordering without launching a harness.
Run `airoute run` with `--dry-run --json` and, for read-only admission, `--read-only`; confirm only adapters declaring native read-only remain.
Inspect state under `~/Library/Application Support/airoute/state`: permissions should be private and events must contain no task text, source, transcript, or credential.
Only after reviewing the dry run, test a real interactive read-only task in the disposable repository. Approve no writes and verify TTY behavior, task handoff, and signal forwarding manually.
Simulate admission/failure behavior with fake local executables, not paid provider calls; verify read-only pre-start fallback, write stop, and no replay after start.

blocks.text: Doctor and dry-run checks are non-spending. A real native interactive launch can consume subscription quota and must be an explicit local decision; this orb did not perform one.
